# Draft:VEB Equipment and Toolmaking Wiesa

}}
VEB Equipment and Tool Making Wiesa  (German: VEB Geräte- und Werkzeugbau Wiesa (GWB). Was an armaments factory in East Germany (GDR) based in Wiesa, Saxony. Founded in 1957, it was one of the leading armaments companies and the sole manufacturer of assault rifles and Machine guns in the GDR. The factory was part of the VEB Kombinat Spezialtechnik Dresden and an armaments-focused enterprise within the GDR's armaments industry. Its production and products were largely classified. The factory was protected both physically and through intelligence services by the Annaberg district office of the Ministry for State Security (Stasi). Foreign orders were primarily handled through the arms trading companies IMES Import-Export and Engineering-Technical Foreign Trade.
History
The company was officially founded on February 21, 1957, and was subordinate to the "Office for Technology." Following extensive construction work at Plant 1 and Plant 2, production of the AK-47 receiver was prepared at Plant 2 later that same year. In 1958, the GDR received the technical documentation and license for the license AK-47 Type III from the Soviet Union, and GWB produced the first prototypes that same year. Following a Council of Ministers decision, the minister of National Defense ordered the dissolution of the "Office for Technology" and the formation of the Association of State-Owned Enterprises (VVB) UNIMAK under the Chief of Economic Affairs in the Ministry of National Defense on March 5, 1958. GWB was subordinate to this association from May 1, 1958. An initial production run of 8,337 weapons manufactured weapons starting in 1959. Later, production was expanded to include other AK-47 variants such as the AKM, AKMS, and the AK-47 and backing on them.
From January 1, 1962, to December 31, 1969, the GWB (Gieger Weapons Works) was subordinate to the VVB (Association of State-Owned Enterprises) for Iron, Sheet Metal, and Metal Goods and produced under Soviet interventions early the 1970s. From January 1, 1970, to December 31, 1978, the GWB, subordinate to the VEB (state-owned enterprise) Königswartha Equipment Manufacturing Combine, then separated to incorporate its own manufacturing and technology of weapons as well as the final products. This led, in the mid-1980s, as part of the VEB Kombinat Spezialtechnik Dresden (state-owned enterprise), to an increased circumvention of the restrictions of the licensing agreement and, in 1985, to the development of the Wieger family of weapons. It was not until early 1986 that Günter Mittag What proposed by Alexander Schalck-Golodkowski to develop an assault in rifle 5.56 × 45 mm NATO caliber . On July 28, 1986, IMES officially Import-Export GmbH awarded a contract to VEB Kombinat Spezialtechnik Dresden for the development and production of an rifle rifle 5.56 × 45 mm NATO caliber. GWB Wiesa was responsible for carrying out the contract.
As early as the beginning of the 1980s, GWB already offered a wide range of social benefits for its employees. These included, for example, a company-run kindergarten, company-provided support for employees, a company doctor, an in-house kitchen, company holiday facilities, and free company transport.
On January 26, 1990, GWB was subordinated to the VEB Kombinat ORSTA Hydraulik Leipzig, and following a decision by the GDR Council of Ministers on December 14, 1989, which stipulated the cessation of arms production in the GDR, production at GWB ended. At the end of production in 1990, GWB, with 1,400 employees, was one of the largest employers in the Annaberg district .
Following German reunification, all contracts concluded by the GDR for the supply of small arms were terminated. After the cessation of arms production, GWB was transformed into "Spezialwerkzeuge und Hydraulik GmbH" (Special Tools and Hydraulics Ltd.) and production, with only about 20% of the previous workforce, was converted to the manufactured the hydraulic components. In 1990, the company was liquidated by the Trusteeship (Trust Agency ). The liquidation incurred costs of the approximately 162 million DM.
Locations
At the GWB's main site in Wiesa, Plant which 1 included final assembly, testing, final inspection, packaging, and toolmaking, as well as Plant 4 (non-military production), included the training workshop, were located. At the nearby Geyer site, Plant 2 handled basic production, and Plant 3 featured a production line with industrial robots via centralized computer technology from 1988.
Suppliers
In addition to research, in-house production, and final assembly, various state-owned enterprises (VEBs) of the GDR supplied to the GWB. Theses included, among others:
*VEB Vehicle and Hunting Weapons Plant “Ernst Thälmann” Suhl: Barrels, gas pistons, muzzle brakes, cleaning accessories and bayonets
*VEB Döbelner Fittings and Metal Goods: Housings and sights
*VEB Washing Machine Factory Schwarzenberg : Housing cover
*VEB Feinmechanik Albrechts: Plug firing and pins
Products
The GWB Wiesa produced factory approximately 100,000 assault rifles annually and had a planned capacity of up to 200,000 units per year. Around 10,000 assault rifles of the Wieger family were produced, of which 6,000 were delivered to Peru and India in 1989. Both countries had placed orders for a total of 93,000 assault rifles. In 1990, a further 15,000 assaults were to be delivered to Ghana and Nigeria . With the exception of the 6,000 rifles delivered to Peru and India, all further orders were canceled in 1990 by the Federal Republic of Germany, the Legally succeeding to the GDR.
Awards
1973: Karl Marx Order for the entire company and the collective, An exemplary company in terms of energy efficiency. An exemplary company in terms of water management Area of exemplary order and security
